South is front-on, with a sagging skull-like face, hollow eye sockets and a gaping, dripping mouth. East is a stooped side profile, head thrust forward and down, back bowed, drips falling from the mouth. North is the back, showing the shoulders, spine region and buttock-like masses, with no face. The heights are visibly equal.
observed.south.png: Front view. The melting face has two dark hollow sockets and a long drooping mouth with goo strings falling down the chest. Thin arms hang at the sides, ending in dripping stubs. observed.east.png: Side profile, strongly hunched and leaning forward as if about to topple. The head hangs low with goo strands from the jaw. The torso sags into bulbous masses over the hips, and the legs are slightly bent and fused with drips. Wet sheen throughout. No support object is drawn.

observed.facings.png: Three facings on one scale: a pear- or teardrop-shaped fleshy sack ending in a twisted, curled stalk at the top. On south and east the lower two thirds are covered in about 20–25 eyeballs set in fleshy sockets. Most irises are amber with vertical slit pupils, others are grey-blue or green with round pupils, and there is one cluster of 3–4 tiny eyes. North shows the same sack with no eyes: wrinkled, veined, mauve-grey skin with folds. All three are the same height and outline.
observed.south.png: Front view of the sack with its stalk curling to the right at the top. A grid of eyes in raised fleshy rims covers the bulging lower body. Eye sizes vary, and so do the irises: amber slit, blue-grey round, green. Most pupils look straight out at the viewer, not upward. The skin is opaque, mauve and veined; the eyes sit on or in the surface rather than showing through a translucent membrane. The edges are clean and there is no backdrop.
observed.east.png: The same sack seen from the side. The stalk leans and curls toward the left, and the body bulges to the right and bottom. It has the same mix of eye sizes and colours, including the tiny-eye cluster on the left flank. Again the eyes face outward toward the camera. The skin is opaque and veined.
observed.north.png: The rear of the sack: the same silhouette and curled stalk, with wrinkled, veined, folded skin and no eyes or face. The painterly rendering matches the other facings.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom beside the vanilla human, the sack is about 0.7 cells, roughly head-and-torso height, sitting in the lower half of its cell. At 32 px per cell it reads as a small pale grey teardrop beside the human and the rat; the eyes become faint speckles.

subject: RM_Gorekite

reply.subject: RM_Gorekite

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. Each shows a broad, ragged-edged, grey-brown membrane shaped like a wide chevron or kite, with curled hooked tips at the two outer corners and on one upper corner. A ridge runs up the centre. The underside is a paler, veined, frilly skirt that converges into one long, glossy, pink-red tentacle hanging below in an S-curve. South and north are near mirror images of each other. East is an oblique three-quarter view with the membrane slanting to the right and the tentacle trailing down-right. The heights look very similar.
observed.south.png: The hide is seen from the front and slightly above: a central raised ridge, small scattered nodules, and two larger round blisters low on the hide either side of the centre. The edges are torn and frilled, the corner tips curl, and the hide is finely veined. A fleshy pink stalk comes out of the underside and becomes a single wet, speckle-highlighted tentacle curling down to a point. There is no head, eyes or mouth. The background is transparent.
observed.east.png: The same hide turned toward the right: it is foreshortened, with the leading edge pointing right and the far corner tips raised at upper left. There are fewer nodules, a veined surface and a ragged trailing margin. The single glossy pink grasper hangs from the underside and sweeps down and to the right. The background is transparent.
observed.north.png: Almost the same picture as south, mirrored: a central ridge, two round blisters, and nodules along the ridge. The curled tip is now at upper right. The underside skirt narrows into the same single wet pink tentacle. There is no face or eyes. The background is transparent.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature spans about 2.3 cells against a human about 1 cell wide, much larger than a person, and the grasper reaches below the hide. At 32 px per cell it reads as a grey triangular sheet with a thin pink trail. That separates from the brown ground, but the contrast is muted.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the hide's leading face toward the camera, symmetric, with the grasper hanging below. The creature has no face by design, and the view is not a profile or rear.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the hide and the trailing grasper with no eyes or face. The two blisters are rounded nodules, not eyes, and they match the ones on south.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: Every facing shows the upper hide at an angle, with the frilly underside skirt and the hanging grasper visible below. None is a flat plan view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 6%, and the panel agrees visually.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Every facing has the same palette, membrane texture, curled tips and single pink grasper. East turns the sheet into a foreshortened oblique view. South and north are near mirrors of each other, which is acceptable for a sheet with no front or back features, but they are barely distinguishable.

SIGNATURE.seen: The stretched, tent-like hide with one long trailing wet grasper is the dominant read on every facing.

ALIEN.seen: The overall kite outline recalls a manta ray, but there are no cephalic lobes, eyes, gill slits or tail. Instead the edges are torn and frilled, the hide is blistered and veined, and a fleshy tentacle replaces the tail. A stranger might say 'ray-like', and most departures are present.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1 present: one flat membrane of hide with no head, eyes or face. 2 present: no wings or fins, the hide itself is the airfoil, taut with curled corners. 3 present: exactly one grasper hangs from beneath, with no paired limbs or tail fins. 4 present: the grasper is glossy pink with specular speckles, against a matte, dry grey hide. 5 largely present: the frilled skirt drapes like a canopy, though the swept chevron outline reads somewhat streamlined and ray-like rather than a slack blanket.

STYLE.seen: Painterly and finely detailed, with veining and soft shading. It is not cel-shaded, cute, photographic or 3D-rendered.

OURS.seen: The bespoke invented creature fits the description. No vanilla or donor art is recognisable.

ALPHA.seen: Clean transparency on all facings, with no ground, shadow or backdrop.

SCALE.seen: At about 2.3 cells wide it is several times the human's width, which fits 'the size of a tent'.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it reads as a grey triangular sheet with a pink trail that separates from the ground. The grey hide's contrast against brown soil is modest.

WINGS_FOLDED.seen: The creature has no wings by design, since the hide is the whole airfoil. Only spread-hide sprites exist and no grounded variant is given, so a folded-wing check does not apply.

findings.seen: The wide chevron outline with curled outer tips is close to a manta ray's wing silhouette when seen at a glance.
findings.quote: Invented creatures and plants read as ALIEN, never as a recoloured Earth species.

reply.image_seen: Five panels show three facings of a wrinkled brown hide canopy with one glossy dangling grasper, plus comparisons beside a human and rat.

concerns.evidence: The curled corners suggest a ray silhouette, but the visible body is a loose, scalloped sheet of hide without a distinct head, eyes, paired wings or fins. One glossy, fleshy grasper hangs beneath the dry membrane. The broad draping canopy and all five required departures are visible; the silhouette resemblance alone does not establish STYLE_EARTHLY.

South and north share the same anatomy but are visibly different drawings: north has a higher upper-right corner, a differently sloping central ridge and lower skirt, and a grasper that curls left before ending toward the right. South's grasper curls right before ending toward the left. Their contours do not match as mirrored copies. A similar broad surface on both views is compatible with this headless membrane body.
